title: Can this reduction be made computationally efficient for sparse matrices

problemStatement.formal: For structured sparse matrices (upper triangular, block triangular, nilpotent), can the Cayley-Hamilton reduction aeval A p = aeval A (p %ₘ charpoly A) be computed efficiently?
problemStatement.plain: The Cayley-Hamilton reduction reduces any polynomial function of a matrix to degree < n. For sparse/structured matrices, can this be done more efficiently than O(n³)?
whyMatters: Upper triangular matrices: charpoly = ∏(X - diagonal), computable in O(n) from diagonal entries
Block triangular matrices: charpoly factors as product of block charpolys — divide-and-conquer
Nilpotent matrices (strictly upper triangular): M^n = 0 reduces the polynomial basis
Diagonal matrices: polynomial evaluation is entry-wise, O(n) per entry

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: CayleyHamiltonReductionOQ01.lean has zero sorries and builds cleanly. Answers the open question 'Can this reduction be made computationally efficient for sparse matrices?' affirmatively for structured sparse matrices: upper triangular, block triangular, nilpotent, and diagonal cases. 14 theorems proved using Mathlib's BlockTriangular.charpoly, charpoly_of_upperTriangular, charpoly_fromBlocks_zero₁₂/₂₁, and aeval_self_charpoly.
builtItems: upper_tri_charpoly_eq_prod: key structural result — O(n) charpoly from diagonal
strictly_upper_tri_nilpotent: M^n = 0 from charpoly = X^n via Cayley-Hamilton
diagonal_pow_diagonal: (D^k) i i = (D i i)^k entry-wise computation
insights: Upper triangular matrices: charpoly is ∏(X - Mᵢᵢ), readable in O(n) from the diagonal
Block triangular: charpoly factorization enables divide-and-conquer reduction
For k blocks of size n/k: block approach costs k × O((n/k)³) vs O(n³), saving factor k²
Strictly upper triangular (zero diagonal) ↔ nilpotent: M^n = 0 trivially from Cayley-Hamilton
Diagonal matrices: polynomial evaluation is entry-wise O(n), no matrix multiplication needed
Matrix.BlockTriangular.charpoly and Matrix.charpoly_of_upperTriangular are the key Mathlib theorems
All results hold over arbitrary commutative rings, not just fields

approaches.name: Structural charpoly factorization + Cayley-Hamilton reduction
approaches.description: Uses Matrix.charpoly_of_upperTriangular (for upper triangular), Matrix.BlockTriangular.charpoly (for block triangular), Matrix.charpoly_fromBlocks_zero₁₂/₂₁ (for 2×2 blocks), and Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly (Cayley-Hamilton) to establish computational efficiency via structural factorization.
